messages:
Maya: Quick heads-up — I ran a replay snapshot using cohort-weighted sampling to validate kernel parity and KV warmup ordering. Need eyes on the diffs.
Liam: Nice. which snapshot and weight profile did you use?
Maya: snapshot s3://redwood-prod/traces/2026-03-10/snap-41 (scrubbed). weight file: weights/cohort-2026-03-10.json, seed=42. command: `./replay --snapshot s3://... --seed 42 --weights weights/cohort-2026-03-10.json --kernels all --kv-warmup=on`
Sophie: Did you apply the new anonymization pipeline (stable-hash + bucketize) or old scrubber?
Maya: stable-hash -> bucketize (keeps consistent cohort mapping across runs). we also removed user-level timestamps and replaced with relative offsets.
Noah: How deterministic were the runs? did you get parity across kernel variants?
Maya: Short summary: across 3 kernel configs (default, tiled-attn, fused-matmul) we saw 99.2% token-level parity for first 512 tokens and p50 latency deltas: default->tiled - 4ms, default->fused +9ms in this bucket. biggest diffs were on KV-replay sequences where warmed entries reordered due to async prefetch.
Liam: 99.2% is promising. can you paste the small repro for the largest delta?
Maya: repro snippet below:
```
# reproduce largest-delta run
./replay \
  --snapshot s3://redwood-prod/traces/2026-03-10/snap-41 \
  --seed 42 \
  --weight-file weights/cohort-2026-03-10.json \
  --kernel fused-matmul \
  --kv-warmup=async_prefetch \
  --out ./replay-output/fused-warmup-run.log
```
Sophie: Did you compare KV warmup sequences? if entries are inserted in different order you'll miss prefix cache parity.
Maya: yes — I diffed KV insert order hashes (we log anonymized keys as `khash(<bucket>, idx)`). most mismatches correlate with requests that have long-lived prefix chains (>3 prefixes).
Noah: Any hypothesis for why fused-matmul increases latency on those? memory backpressure on prefetch threads?
Maya: probably. fused matmul increases mem copies in our path, and async prefetch contends for the same allocator pool. also kernel scheduling bumped the kv-prefetch timing by one tick which changes insert ordering.
Liam: Can we make the replay harness force a canonical KV insertion ordering to test? e.g., serialize warmup or use deterministic prefetch scheduling.
Maya: I added a flag `--kv-warmup-mode={serial,async,deterministic}` and ran deterministic where prefetch uses a seeded RNG to pick reorder but applied a fixed sorting pass before insertion. That bumped parity to 99.98% for the same cohort sample.
Sophie: Nice. did you keep sample weighting? We need apples-to-apples: same random seed + same weight distribution.
Maya: yes — weights unchanged. I also bucketed traffic by seq-len and user-cohort so comparisons don't mix load profiles.
Noah: what about end-to-end perf metrics (p99/p95)?
Maya: p95 stable, p99 had 12ms tail wobble on fused-matmul with async prefetch. I attached small histogram excerpt in the run logs (lines 230-260) showing spikes aligned with concurrent KV GC.
Liam: sounds like next steps: 1) run deterministic-kv across all kernels for 24h job, 2) rerun with serial warmup to confirm baseline, 3) add a small micro-benchmark to isolate allocator contention.
Maya: agreed. I'll kick off 24h deterministic-kv jobs across all kernels and post results.
replay-bot: job 2961234578 started (deterministic-kv sweep) — ETA 24h :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Sophie: also file an infra perf trace for the fused-matmul GC/alloc windows so we can get flamegraphs.
Maya: on it. I'll annotate the replay run with the trace id.
Noah: cool. if deterministic run keeps parity high, we can push a kernel-fallback policy that prefers deterministic-warmup for canary lanes.
Maya: noted — will include a short proposal with numbers once runs finish. :thumbsup:
